## Requirements Quality

- [ ] CHK001 Requirements describe what users need and why, not implementation
      choices
- [ ] CHK002 Acceptance scenarios are independently testable
- [ ] CHK003 Success criteria are measurable and technology-agnostic
- [ ] CHK004 Assumptions and out-of-scope items are explicit

## Security and Privacy

- [ ] CHK005 Sensitive data, auth/authz, abuse cases, and input validation are
      addressed or explicitly marked N/A
- [ ] CHK006 Secrets, credentials, logs, external connectors, and generated code
      risks are addressed or explicitly marked N/A

## Testing Strategy

- [ ] CHK007 Unit, contract, integration, and E2E coverage is chosen by risk
- [ ] CHK008 Manual verification is documented only where automation is not
      practical in scope
- [ ] CHK009 Regression-prone behavior has a named validation path

## UX, Accessibility, and Operations

- [ ] CHK010 User-facing changes account for accessibility, loading, empty,
      error, and destructive states
- [ ] CHK011 Operational needs such as logging, monitoring, support, and runbook
      ownership are addressed or explicitly marked N/A

## Performance and Traceability

- [ ] CHK012 Performance, scale, memory, rendering, startup, or cost budgets are
      defined where relevant
- [ ] CHK013 Material decisions have an ADR or a documented waiver
- [ ] CHK014 The feature can be traced from requirement to plan to task to
      validation evidence

## Notes

- Check items off as completed: `[x]`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
